Android Auto isn’t accepting the connection. In its settings: tap \"Version\" about ten times to unlock developer settings, then, in the ⋮ menu, tap \"Start head unit server\". After you restart the phone, you need to turn it on again.

The Android Auto app menu gets a fit of its own, used while the menu is on screen; other apps keep the fit of the other tab. The switch is automatic and relies on REau’s Accessibility service: without it, the menu uses the apps’ fit.
The app menu uses the same fit as the apps. Turn on the switch above to give it its own.
Android may pause REau while the screen is off to save battery. Exclude REau from battery optimization so the projection doesn’t drop.

Battery saver is on: with the screen off, Android cuts the network and location for background apps. REau keeps going thanks to its pinned notification; if the dash or Android Auto drops, turn battery saver off.
Dash mask: darkens what doesn’t reach the dash’s round glass, using the fit chosen below, and shows where the dash ring is

Gemini by joystick: it listens through the helmet’s Bluetooth headset (or, without one, the phone’s microphone). Asks for microphone permission. This switch is what makes the \"Gemini\" action on the Joystick page work. Applies the next time you turn on
View only: touch here doesn’t reach Android Auto. The dash keeps receiving the picture normally.
Android Auto isn’t installed on this phone. Tap \"Get Android Auto\" to install it from Google Play, open it once to finish its setup, then come back.
Android Auto isn’t installed, and this phone has no app store or browser to get it from.
Couldn’t open Android Auto’s settings. Open Android Auto from your app list.
Open REau and type the full name in Settings

The dash only accepts its full Wi-Fi name (for example RE_AB12_345678), and REau couldn’t find it: Android only lets apps scan for networks while REau is open on screen. Open Settings, tap Forget, then type the full name in the Full Wi-Fi name field; or turn on the projection with REau open.
Another app is using the dash (the phone’s port 2002 is busy): probably another dash app that’s streaming. Turn off its streaming; REau tries again on its own.

With the projection on, the settings tagged LIVE apply right away (language, theme, using the location, answering calls, phone status, album art, real route on the dash, the diagnostic log, the detailed log and deleting the oldest automatically), the weather switch on the Weather screen and, on the Android Auto screen, so do fit, crop, position and the FPS and bitrate text. Density and margins do too, but they restart Android Auto (the picture freezes for a few seconds). On the network server screen, the switches and the sound choice also apply right away (changing between Phone and the others restarts Android Auto for a moment). Every other setting applies the next time you turn on.
From Android Auto: %1$s → on the dash: %2$s
the chosen part falls outside the Android Auto frame
the picture falls outside the dash frame
the picture would be too small
nothing would show on the glass

REau’s theme is the day and night signal it sends to Android Auto. Light and Dark fix the theme. By the sun: light from sunrise to sunset, dark at night; the sun times come from the phone’s position if \"Use location\" is on, or from the time zone (around 6 AM and 6 PM) if not. Waze and other apps follow only if their theme is set to automatic.

Android joins the dash’s Wi-Fi on its own when it appears, without the network picker and without REau having to look for the network. Android asks once whether you accept the network suggested by REau. Only works once the full dash name is known.
Record the video sent to the dash

Answer calls by joystick (in both dash modes): with the phone ringing, one tap on the left answers and one tap on the right or center declines; during a call, one tap on the center hangs up (the dash doesn’t send left or right during a call); also works for WhatsApp and other voice apps, through Android Auto (asks for phone permissions)
Detailed log: every dash packet and every Android Auto message in the log (much larger file; without the route card text). It only records while the diagnostic log is on.
Dash Wi-Fi \'%1$s\' not found nearby — check that it’s on and in range
Couldn’t connect to \'%1$s\' — the network shows up, but the connection failed: wrong password, the Android prompt was declined, or it timed out
Couldn’t connect to \'%1$s\' — network not found or wrong password

The dash Wi-Fi \'%1$s\' is refusing the connection. If the password is still the panel’s default one, the dash has frozen: turn the motorcycle off with the ignition key, wait about 30 seconds and turn it back on; REau keeps trying on its own
Android Auto is closing the previous session

Android Auto is still closing the previous session. It takes up to about 1 minute and REau tries again by itself. To skip the wait, in Android Auto’s settings, stop and start the head unit server again.
Android Auto is connected but isn’t sending a picture, and the dash stays black. Force stop it (Settings › Apps › Android Auto › Force stop); if REau says the server is off, tap Try again.
Android Auto accepts the connection but doesn’t respond. Force stop it (Settings › Apps › Android Auto › Force stop); REau tries again by itself.

Android Auto accepts the connection but doesn’t respond. In Android Auto’s developer settings, tap ⋮ and choose \"Stop head unit server\", then ⋮ and \"Start head unit server\"; REau tries again by itself.

%1$s is also installed on this phone and may be using Android Auto: its head unit server takes only one session at a time. If it is on, turn it off (tap Turn off in it), wait about a minute and REau connects by itself.
Choose what each joystick tap does. Applies right away, even while the projection is on.
Calls, in both modes: while ringing, left answers and right or center declines; during a call, center hangs up. Needs the \"Answer calls\" switch.

Turn the Android Auto server on and off automatically (needs accessibility). With the phone unlocked, it opens the Android Auto menu behind a cover and taps \"Start head unit server\"; when the projection ends, it turns the server off. Android Auto developer mode must be on (you do the 10 taps on \"Version\" yourself). With accessibility allowed, some apps, such as banking apps, may refuse to open. Applies the next time you turn the projection on or off.
REau accessibility: on, but not connected yet (turn it off and on again in Accessibility if it stays this way)

To turn the server on automatically, enable REau in Accessibility. On Android 13 or newer, if REau was installed from outside the Play Store, first allow it in Settings › Apps › REau › ⋮ › \"Allow restricted settings\".

REau uses Android’s Accessibility service to turn the Android Auto server on automatically. With Accessibility allowed, some apps, such as banking apps, may refuse to open or stop working because they treat this feature as a risk. If that happens, turn off REau’s Accessibility in Android’s settings. Continue?
Turning on the Android Auto server…
Turning off the Android Auto server…
Turning off the Android Auto server…
Turning on the Android Auto server…
To turn the server on automatically, enable REau in Accessibility.
Unlock the phone and tap Try again: Android Auto settings won’t open with the screen locked.
Android Auto settings weren’t found on this phone.
Android Auto opened a different screen. Open Android Auto, deal with what it asks and try again.
The Android Auto menu didn’t open in time. Try again or turn it on manually: ⋮ → Start head unit server.
Android Auto developer mode is off. Tap \"Open Android Auto settings\", scroll to the bottom, tap \"Version\" 10 times, confirm, then come back and tap Try again.
This version of Android Auto changed the server menu. Turn it on manually: ⋮ → Start head unit server.
The Android Auto server is marked as on and didn’t respond. Tap Stop and then Start in the Android Auto menu, or force stop Android Auto.
Android Auto didn’t start the server. Try again.
The Android Auto server was left on (the phone was locked or REau’s accessibility service was off). Turn it off from its notification, if you like.

Everything REau can use on the phone, whether it’s allowed and what for. What leaves the phone goes to the dash, over the dash’s Wi-Fi, and, only with \"Turn on the network server\" on, to your network; the only trip to the internet is \"Weather on the dash\". More in \"REau and your data\".
Special access (you turn these on yourself)
Up to you (Android asks, or you allow them in settings)
On, but stuck (Android says \"not working\"): turn it off and on again

Reads which screen Android Auto is showing (apps menu, Waze, Google Maps…) to switch the picture fit on the dash automatically and, with the \"Turn on the server automatically\" switch, to turn its server on and off. It only listens to Android Auto, Google Maps and calls from WhatsApp, Telegram and Signal.
Without this, Android may pause REau with the screen off and the projection drops. It isn’t a permission: it’s the list of apps Android lets run in the background.
The pinned projection notification, with its Turn off button. Requested when you turn on the projection (Android 13 or newer).
Answer and hang up calls with the dash joystick. Requested only with the \"Answer calls\" switch.

Know whether the phone is ringing or in a call, so the joystick acts at the right time. Requested together with the previous one; REau doesn’t read numbers or the call list (the caller’s name comes from Android Auto).
Gemini by joystick: your voice goes from the helmet’s Bluetooth headset (or the phone) to Android Auto. Requested only with the \"Gemini\" switch. REau doesn’t store the audio.

To list Wi-Fi networks and find the dash’s full Wi-Fi name automatically: Android only returns the list with this permission. Requested when REau doesn’t know the name yet, without reading your position. Your position is only read with the \"Use location\" switch on, for the sun-based theme.

The name is misleading: Android requires it for any connection. REau talks to the dash over its Wi-Fi (no internet) and to Android Auto inside the phone (127.0.0.1). Only \"Weather on the dash\", off by default, actually goes online (Open-Meteo).
Know whether the dash Wi-Fi is connected and notice when it drops, to reconnect.
Find the dash network (the name starts with RE_) and check which Wi-Fi the phone is connected to.
Ask Android to connect to the dash Wi-Fi and, with automatic connection on, leave it as a suggested network.
Ask Android for the dash network, even without internet, and tie the dash connection to it; the rest of the phone stays on 4G.
The projection runs as a foreground service, with the pinned notification, so it keeps going with the screen off.
The service type Android has required for the projection since Android 14: the motorcycle’s dash is a connected device.
The same service with the microphone type, only for Gemini by joystick: without it Android delivers silence with the screen off.
Keep the processor and Wi-Fi awake with the screen off while the projection is on; released when it turns off.
Choose the Bluetooth headset’s microphone for Gemini by joystick.
Show Android’s request to take REau out of battery optimization (the special access above). On its own it changes nothing.
Added by an Android library (AndroidX) that REau uses, to protect the app’s internal notices. It gives access to nothing on the phone.

Diagnostic log (on by default): records on the phone itself what happens in REau, to find bugs later; nothing leaves the phone unless you share it. When off, REau records nothing (neither the detailed log nor the copy of the system messages about REau); what was already recorded stays until you delete it (or until the period set in \"Automatically delete\" ends)
Deletes all the logs stored on the phone and the last shared file. If the log is on, it starts again in a new file. This can’t be undone.
Deletes all the logs stored on the phone, the last shared file and the recordings of the video and of the Android Auto sessions. If the log is on, it starts again in a new file. This can’t be undone.

A local bridge between the phone’s Android Auto and the motorcycle’s dash: it receives the picture (and, if you want, the music, who’s calling and the joystick), adapts it and sends it to the dash over its Wi-Fi.

To the dash, over the dash’s Wi-Fi: the picture and, with the switches on, the music and who’s calling. The Wi-Fi is protected by the dash’s password; the picture has no other encryption. Only with \"Weather on the dash\" on (off by default) does REau query Open-Meteo over the internet, with the position rounded to about 11 km. Otherwise, it doesn’t use the internet.
The browser (only if you turn it on)

Only with \"Turn on the network server\" on (off by default): anyone on the same network who enters the PIN sees the Android Auto picture (and hears the sound, if you choose; with the touch switch, they can also tap). Traffic isn’t encrypted and doesn’t go through the internet; don’t turn it on in networks shared with strangers. It turns off on its own when Android Auto ends.

The diagnostic log, without your position, streets, songs or who’s calling (for WhatsApp, Telegram and Signal calls, only the app and the buttons) and, if you turn them on, the debug recordings, which keep the map image. Everything stays in the app’s folder and only leaves through \"Share\" (Settings → Debug).
What REau remembers about the dash

The dash’s Wi-Fi name and password and what the dash has already told REau (its settings, versions and range), encrypted with a key kept by Android. If you turn them on, also the rounded position (about 11 km) and the last weather, in the app’s folder.

In Settings → Debug: turn off the log and, under \"Delete\", delete the logs or the logs and recordings. Music and who’s calling are turned off in Settings → On the dash. Permissions and what they are for are in the \"Permissions\" shortcut on the home screen.
What reaches Android Auto belongs to it: your voice in Gemini and Waze routes follow Google’s and Waze’s rules, not REau’s.

REau is an independent project, not affiliated with Royal Enfield or Google; Royal Enfield and Tripper may be trademarks of their respective owners, and the other names mentioned belong to theirs. It exists because these projects opened the way first. Tap one to copy its address.

Asks at once for the permissions Android prompts for; accessibility and battery have their own buttons on their rows. If Android doesn’t show the request (you declined before), use \"Open REau’s permissions in Android\".

Use location (off by default): with the theme set by the sun, to know the sunrise and sunset times where you are. This position is the last one Android already has, read when you open REau, without turning on GPS; it stays on the phone only, rounded to about 11 km, and never goes to the log or leaves the phone. When off, REau forgets the saved position. With the projection on and the theme set by the sun, the dash takes the change right away. Android’s location permission also lets REau see the list of Wi-Fi networks to find the dash, whether this switch is on or not; for that it doesn’t read your position.

Automatically deletes the log and recordings older than the chosen time (applies right away when you choose, and again when you open the app and with each new file). Past 200 MB, the oldest logs go first whatever you choose; recordings have their own ceiling, also 200 MB.
Showing the end of the file; the beginning was left out (in KB: %1$d). The whole file leaves through \"Share the logs\".

A VPN is holding REau back
With REau inside the VPN, Android won’t let it use the dash’s Wi-Fi. In the VPN app, leave REau out (\"split tunneling\") and fully reconnect the VPN.
Applies right away with the projection on. The rest applies the next time you turn on.

This is the dash whose full Wi-Fi name REau already knows, which it needs to connect. \"Forget\" deletes that name, everything the dash has reported (the bike data below) and the network suggested to Android. After that, REau looks for the dash again (with REau open, the name shows up on its own) or you type the full name. Use it when you change motorcycle or dash.

REau doesn’t know your dash’s full Wi-Fi name yet, and without it the dash won’t accept the connection. To find it automatically, Android requires the location permission: REau uses it only to see the list of Wi-Fi networks, never your position. Or type the full name below. If there is more than one dash nearby, check the name and use Forget.
Looking for the dash’s Wi-Fi… Turn on the motorcycle near the phone, with REau open: the name will appear here on its own.
Allow location (only to find the Wi-Fi)
As it appears in the phone’s Wi-Fi list, for example RE_AB12_345678
Your position, for the sun-based theme
Light by day, dark at night, by the sun
Title, album and artist on the dash
Caller’s name (or number) on the dash
Off: you turn it on manually
Turns on and off with the projection

Android Auto draws its screen in a smaller area, centered in its 800 × 480 frame, with black around it; the margin is how much is taken off the width (or the height), split evenly between the two sides. That way the picture already comes out in the shape the dash needs, with nothing cut off afterwards. Applies right away, but restarts Android Auto: the picture freezes for a few seconds.

REau uses two fixed video profiles for the dash. Profile A: %1$d fps and %2$d kbps, the smoother picture. Profile B: half of that (%3$d fps and %4$d kbps), lighter on the Wi-Fi and the dash. The maneuver profile and the speed profile, just below, choose between them. These values can’t be changed.
Profile A: 400 kbps. Profile B: %1$d kbps. Fixed

Picks the video profile by the distance to the route’s next maneuver: within 1 km of it, A; farther away, B, once the distance has changed by about 200 m (so it doesn’t keep switching). It only decides while a route is active. If the speed profile asks for B, B wins.

Picks the video profile by the route’s speed: up to about 55 km/h, A; from about 65 km/h, B; in between it stays as it was. It only decides while a route is active. If the maneuver profile asks for B, B wins.

The wallpaper is a still picture the dash shows in place of Android Auto; it starts with the \"Send wallpaper\" button on the home screen. The picture shows whole, unstretched, centered, with black around it (the ideal size is 526 × 300). REau keeps only the picture’s address, not a copy: if you delete or move the file, the dash shows a REau test card instead. \"Reset to default\" brings back the test picture. A change applies the next time the wallpaper starts.
FPS and bitrate on the video

Draws the frames per second and the bitrate of the last 5 s over the dash video, in red with a black outline (e.g. \"3.8 fps 187 kbps\"). When on, the position (X and Y) and the text size appear here. Applies right away with the projection on. For testing: the text sits over the map.
FPS and bitrate on the video
Another device opens the address in a browser

With the projection running, REau opens a server on the local network: a computer or car display with a browser, on the same network, opens the address, enters the 4-digit PIN and sees Android Auto. When on, REau doesn’t look for the dash. The PIN changes every time; after 5 wrong attempts the device waits 5 minutes. The picture is sent unencrypted. Two browsers at most. It turns itself off when the projection ends.
Without this, the browser can only watch
With the switch on, the browser can also tap the Android Auto screen: open apps, make and answer calls, change the route. Turn it on only on a network you trust.

Phone: sound stays on the phone only (Waze’s voice goes to the helmet headset). Browser: sound goes only to the browser and the phone is silent (with \"Turn on the network server\" off, the phone plays). Both: both play. Switching between Phone and the other options restarts Android Auto for a moment. The browser only plays after a tap on the page.
The address and PIN appear in a moment, once the server is on.
This phone isn’t on any local network right now. Connect to a Wi-Fi network to get an address.
Anyone with this address and the PIN, on the same network, can see the Android Auto screen (map, route, who’s calling).

Keeps on the phone a copy of the video sent to the dash (the first 3000 frames of each stream), with the map it shows. It’s for investigating picture problems. It stays in the app’s folder and only leaves if you use \"Share › With recordings\". Recordings add up to 200 MB at most: past that, the oldest go. Applies the next time you turn on.
Saves the map and the route

Records everything Android Auto sends in one connection (the map picture, the route and the messages), up to 100 MB per connection, to study later. It reveals where you rode: it stays in the app’s folder and only leaves if you use \"Share › With recordings\". Recordings add up to 200 MB at most: past that, the oldest go. Applies the next time you turn on.
Leaves the phone only when you tap here
Right away, when the app opens and with each new file
Cap: 200 MB of logs and 200 MB of recordings
Tap and drag on the picture to use Android Auto. The dash still receives it.
Larger = bigger text and buttons. One value for the menu and the apps; changing it restarts the session.
The menu uses the settings below

Fill the dome: Android Auto’s picture is as large as possible inside the dash area; the corners may end up behind the glass’s round edge. Whole image: smaller, so no part is hidden by the round edge. Center crop: takes only a middle part and enlarges it as far as the dash allows; the crop’s size and place are the settings below. The Mask, at the top, darkens what doesn’t reach the glass and shows where the dash ring is. Applies right away.
In map mode, the up arrow is the dash’s own back button: it asks whether you want to exit navigation. REau sends no action for it.
In map mode, the center button puts the dash in media control. It can’t be changed.
During calls the buttons are fixed and the same in both dash modes: here you can only see what each one does. Needs the \"Answer calls\" switch.
The dash doesn’t send this tap
Applies to carrier calls and to WhatsApp and other voice apps.
If the helmet intercom answers first (after about 7.5 s of ringing), this tap hangs up the call that was already answered. While ringing, center doesn’t play or pause the music.
Applies to carrier calls and WhatsApp. After it acts, the same button is ignored for 3 s, so an accidental repeat tap does nothing.
One step per tap; the helmet follows.
While ringing, up and down stay as they are in the mode the dash is in (Map mode or Media control).
During a call the dash keeps left and right for itself: REau doesn’t receive those taps.

If Android says \"Restricted setting\" when you turn it on: tap \"Allow restricted settings\" below, then tap ⋮ in the corner and choose \"Allow restricted settings\". Then go back and turn on accessibility. This happens on Android 13 or newer when REau was installed from a file, outside the Play Store.
Uses the internet only for weather, if you turn it on.
Sends data only to your motorcycle’s dash.
The log stays on the phone, without your location.
REau is free software under the AGPL-3.0. Its source code is published here: tap to copy the address.
Takes a few seconds. No need to tap anything.
Signal, battery and GPS on the dash

Sends the dash the phone’s real status: the battery (and whether it’s charging), whether GPS is on and whether there’s network signal. When off, the dash always shows the same fixed values (battery at 62 percent, not charging, GPS on, signal present), which say nothing about the phone. Applies right away.
The image on the music card
Sends the album art to the dash’s music card (a small image, 75 by 75). It only shows with \"Now playing\" on and a song playing. Applies right away (the art shows at the next song or card update).
Experimental: time left and next turn

Sends the dash the time left on the route and the turn after the next one (only within 100 m of it). When rerouting with no internet, it shows the no-signal icon. When off, the dash keeps the fixed values it had before. Applies right away (the route updates the dash at each Android Auto notice).

When the dash last told REau something. Everything on this screen comes from the dash; REau only shows it and never changes anything on it. \"Not reported yet\" means the dash hasn’t sent that item yet: REau asks when it connects and again every 15 minutes while the projection is on, and some notices only come when something changes on the bike. Forgetting the dash clears all of this.
On (the dash asks for an update)

How far the bike can still go on the fuel it has, as the dash itself counts it: REau only shows the number the dash sends (about every 5 seconds) and never changes anything on it. REau reads it as kilometres; with the dash set to miles, it is converted here and the kilometres stay in brackets. It falls as you ride and jumps up when you refuel. With the bike off or the dash out of reach, you see the last value it said, and the line below tells when. Forgetting the dash clears it.
Temperature and weather icon, over the internet

When off, the dash gets no temperature or weather icon. When on, REau queries the Open-Meteo service every time you open REau and then every 15 minutes, and sends the dash the current temperature and the icon: sun, cloudy, rain, storm or snow. Needs \"Use location\" on and an internet connection on the phone. With no internet, the last known weather is used for up to 3 hours; after that the dash shows none. When you turn it off, the stored weather is deleted. Note: the temperature in the dash’s top bar comes from the motorcycle’s own thermometer. REau’s weather goes to the dash, but that bar still shows the bike’s. What you see here is the weather service’s.
No location: turn on \"Use location\" (Settings → Theme) and open REau once
No internet on the phone right now; the last weather is used for up to 3 hours
The weather service didn’t respond; the last weather is used for up to 3 hours
Nothing: no temperature and no icon on the dash
No protection needed for most activities
Network server on. Tap to see the data.
Network server off. Tap to see the data.

Shows Android Auto away from the dash: with the network server on, a computer or an old car stereo with a browser, on the same network, opens the address, enters the PIN, and sees and taps Android Auto. While it’s on, REau doesn’t look for the dash, because the goal is to run on something other than the dash; when it’s off, REau looks for the dash again. You also choose here where the sound goes.
You can now open the address on the network.
Turn on below to appear on the network.
On the home screen, tap Turn on, then turn on here.
While on, REau does not look for the dash.
On the home screen, tap Turn on first.
Open Android Auto, finish its setup, then turn REau off and on again
Open Android Auto and finish its setup
REau asked Android Auto (17.3 or older) to connect and it didn’t. Open Android Auto, finish its setup and accept what it asks, then turn REau off and on again.
